title: NSC 104 - Nursing Procedures and Clinical Practice

items.q: Which of the following best describes Weaning?
o: the process by which the baby and placenta are pushed out of the womb
the gradual introduction of solid food into a baby's diet
the physical or chemical restriction of a patient's movement for safety
a disease that cannot be cured and will end in the death of the patient
items.s: Weaning: the gradual introduction of solid food into a baby's diet. The other options describe Terminal illness, Restraint, Labour.

items.s: Nasogastric tube: a tube passed through the nose into the stomach for feeding or drainage. The other options describe Oral rehydration solution, Specimen, Scope of practice.

items.s: Last offices: the care given to the body of a patient after death. The other options describe Delegation, Specimen, Cold compress.
